fix.shows: From the lists of names left off Maharashtra's draft roll for all 288 constituencies, the Sabar Institute counts 2,06,88,421 names, 21.1% of the 9,78,54,049 electors on the roll before the revision, and finds 16.8% of them marked dead. It describes the other 1,72,06,190, marked permanently shifted, untraceable or absent, or already enrolled elsewhere, as alive. It reports that Mumbai's 36 constituencies have 11% of the state's electors and 17% of the names, that in Colaba more names were left off than votes were cast in 2024, and that names left off for a reason other than death exceed the 2024 winning margin in 190 of the 288 seats. It finds 3,250 of the 6,101 third gender electors on the 2024 roll, 53.3%, on the lists. Outside Mumbai, among electors aged 18 to 29 marked permanently shifted, it counts 8,22,798 women and 3,79,991 men, which it reads as consistent with women moving to a husband's home after marriage. The roll has no column for religion, and Sabar classifies the names by religion itself. By that classification Muslim names are 14.6% of the names left off, against about 12.1% expected from the 2011 Census, and the odds of a Muslim name being marked already enrolled elsewhere, against being marked dead, are 2.07 times those of other names of the same age in the same seat. The report says name matching for duplicates may be one cause, which the lists do not let it test, and that none of this proves any group was targeted. It finds no difference between the seats of the two alliances once Mumbai, region, reservation, urbanisation and size are allowed for, and the strongest link is with low turnout in 2024. The office of Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer replied on 7 November that electors marked dead or already enrolled are a little over 25% of the names and those marked absent or shifted about 75%, that comparing Mumbai and Thane with the state average is not appropriate, and that the revision is still under way, PTI reported.

note: Second reading, 8 November 2026 (second reader): the report's page opened again through a rendering scrape (dated November 7, 2026, authors Sabir Ahamed, Ashin Chakraborty and Souptik Halder) and the PDF downloaded again from its link and read with pdftotext, pages 1 to 16 and the conclusion on page 305. Title, outlet, date, authors and type checked. Checked against the report: 2,06,88,421 names, 21.1% of 9,78,54,049, 16.8% marked dead, 1,72,06,190 non-death names, Mumbai's 36 seats with 11% of electors and 17% of names, Colaba 1,19,606 against 1,18,499 votes (1.01 times), 190 of 288 seats, 3,250 of 6,101 third gender electors (53.3%), 8,22,798 women and 3,79,991 men aged 18 to 29 marked shifted outside Mumbai and the marriage reading, 14.6% Muslim names by its name-based classification against a census expectation of about 12.1%, the odds ratio of 2.07, the alliance difference of minus 0.27 points (p = 0.82) after the five controls, and turnout as the strongest predictor (rho = minus 0.81). Both quotes are verbatim from the executive summary. The Chief Electoral Officer's reply checked against PTI in Vartha Bharati (2026-11-07T23:42:24+05:30): a little over 25 per cent dead and already enrolled, around 75 per cent absent or shifted, Mumbai and Thane against the state average, and the exercise still under way. Corrected: the odds ratio is the odds of being marked already enrolled against being marked dead, as the report's table and executive summary give it, and the summary now says so. The report's caution is now in its own words, that name-based duplicate matching is one possible mechanism the lists do not let it test and that none of this proves any group was targeted. The summary attributes every figure to Sabar, says the religion classification is Sabar's own, and carries no conclusion about intent.
